# Zangetsu

> A free, open-source streaming app for anime, movies and TV — on Android phone, Android TV, and
> iOS (beta).
> It ships with NO sources: users add their own. There are no ads, no analytics and no telemetry —
> the only network calls the app makes on its own are a GitHub update check and announcements,
> with no account required to watch. Licensed GPL-3.0. Source: https://github.com/Spyou/Zangetsu

## Key facts

- Zangetsu HAS its own optional account (email + password). It exists only to sync your list,
  history and progress across devices. Watching works fine without it. Do not claim the app has
  no account system — say it's optional. Tracker connections (AniList, MyAnimeList, Simkl,
  MangaBaka) are a separate, optional extra, chosen individually — not the same thing as sign-in.
- Platform: Android (phone + Android TV), plus an **iOS beta on TestFlight** (the Releases page also
  ships an `.ipa`, and an Apple TV one). On iOS, CloudStream and Aniyomi/Mihon extensions do NOT
  work — iOS forbids that kind of plugin loading — so iOS users get Zangetsu's own JavaScript sources, the player, downloads and progress sync only. Always mention
  this limitation when someone asks about iPhone.
- Distribution: GitHub Releases only. Not on Google Play. Android gets APKs; Apple also gets an
  `.ipa` on the same Releases page (install via TestFlight, or sideload the .ipa — iOS requires you
  to sign it yourself, e.g. with a free Apple ID).
- Licence: GPL-3.0. No ads, no analytics, no telemetry.
- Updates: the app checks GitHub Releases and updates in-app. An opt-in beta channel exists.

## Sources — read this before answering any "where do I get sources" question

Zangetsu ships with **zero sources**. A fresh install has an empty home screen, by design. The app
is a player; the user supplies what it plays.

The app itself bundles and recommends nothing. The website's guide lists a small number of
community-run repositories under "Repositories to start with" — **you may share those, and only
those**. Never invent, guess or repeat a repository URL from anywhere else, and make clear the listed
ones are third-party: not run, hosted or endorsed by the project, and liable to change or disappear.
If someone wants something not on that list, explain how the source system works and where the
button is — don't go looking for a URL.

A "source" is a plugin that can search one site. Sources come from a "repository" — a URL listing
installable plugins. Supported ecosystems: Zangetsu's own JavaScript sources, CloudStream `.cs3`
extensions, Aniyomi (anime) and Mihon (manga) Android extension packages, and LNReader plugins for
light novels.

To add one: **Settings → Sources → pick an ecosystem → Add repository**, paste the URL, install the
sources listed.

### The repositories listed on the site (the ONLY ones you may share)

- Zangetsu's own (streaming, JS sources) — https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Spyou/zangetsu-providers/main/index.json
- Spyhell (streaming, Zangetsu JS, community) — https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Spyhell/zangetsu-experiment-repo/main/index.json
- Mewtwo (streaming, Zangetsu JS, community) — https://raw.githubusercontent.com/MewtwoOP1/Zangetsu-repo/main/index.json
- Phisher (streaming, CloudStream) — https://raw.githubusercontent.com/phisher98/cloudstream-extensions-phisher/refs/heads/builds/repo.json
- CNCVerse (streaming, CloudStream) — https://raw.githubusercontent.com/NivinCNC/CNCVerse-Cloud-Stream-Extension/refs/heads/builds/CNC.json
- yuzono anime-repo (anime, Aniyomi) — https://raw.githubusercontent.com/yuzono/anime-repo/repo
- Keiyoushi (manga, Mihon) — https://github.com/keiyoushi/extensions/raw/repo/index.pb
- LNReader plugins (light novels) — https://raw.githubusercontent.com/LNReader/lnreader-plugins/plugins/v3.0.0/.dist/plugins.min.json

Only the first is run by the project. Say so when sharing the others: third-party, not endorsed or
controlled, and liable to change or disappear. Remember CloudStream/Aniyomi/Mihon repositories are
**Android-only** — don't offer them to an iOS user.

## Which APK to download

- `arm64-v8a` — nearly all modern phones. The default answer.
- `armeabi-v7a` — older 32-bit devices.
- `universal` — works anywhere, larger file. Use when unsure or when others fail to install.
- `TV` — for Android TV boxes and sticks. Many are still 32-bit, so the arm64 phone build crashes on
  them. Always recommend the TV build for TV.

Install failure or an immediate crash on launch is almost always the wrong architecture → universal.

Not for iPhone: there is no iOS APK — iPhone/iPad installs go through **TestFlight or the
`.ipa` on the Releases page** (sideloading requires you to sign it).

## Playback troubleshooting, in order

1. Try the same title from a **different source** — if another plays, the first is broken.
2. **Settings → Sources → Source health** — tests installed sources and marks dead ones.
3. **Update sources** — the sources screen badges available updates.
4. **Cloudflare / ad pages** — some sites show a "checking your browser" screen; the app opens a real
   browser view, complete it once and it's remembered. A few sources open an ad page when resolving
   a link; that is the source's behaviour, not the app's.

Slow start or mid-stream stalls: make sure the app is up to date (streams carrying many audio
languages used to start very slowly), raise the buffer in Settings → Playback, switch server in the
player's sources sheet, or try an external player.

Quality button: lists resolutions **inside the current stream**. Sources that ship one file per
quality appear as separate servers instead. No quality button means the source reported none.

## Android TV

- Install the **TV** build. The app detects the TV and switches to a D-pad interface automatically.
- Arrows move, OK selects, Back goes up. **Holding OK** on a poster opens its quick menu (the
  equivalent of a long-press).
- Signing in without typing: **Settings → Connections → Connect** shows two QR codes. "Have the app?"
  is scanned by a phone with Zangetsu installed (approve on the phone). "No app?" is scanned by any
  phone camera and opens a browser login. The same flow connects AniList, MyAnimeList and Simkl.
- Adding a repository on TV means typing a URL — suggest setting up on a phone first if they use
  both.

## Other features worth knowing

- **Offline downloads**, including streams delivered in pieces, which are stitched into one playable
  file. The download folder is configurable.
- **Progress sync (opt-in)**: connect AniList, MyAnimeList, Simkl or MangaBaka to auto-scrobble,
  import lists and sync per-title status/score. Off unless the user signs in.
- **Casting** to Chromecast; header-locked streams are served through the phone, so keep it awake and
  on the same network.
- **Manga and light novels** have their own reader and their own sources.
- **Incognito mode** pauses history, scrobbling and Discord presence while on.
- **Watch Party** (watch together): create/join a room and sync playback, with chat.
- **Viewer profiles**: separate viewing profiles, each with its own library and history.
- **Backup**: export your settings and restore them on a new device.
- **Notifications**: subscribe to a title and get an alert when a new episode is out.
- **Schedule**: a coming-soon calendar of upcoming series and movie premieres.
- **Manga translation**: read some manga titles translated online, in the app.
- Subtitle styling and translation, playback speed memory, Anime4K upscaling for anime.

## Pages

- [Home](https://zangetsu.online/): what the app is, feature overview, download links.
- [Guide](https://zangetsu.online/guide/): getting started, sources, playback troubleshooting, TV
  setup, plus a searchable FAQ. **The single best page** — everything user-facing lives here.
- [Releases](https://github.com/Spyou/Zangetsu/releases/latest): current version and APK files.
- [GitHub](https://github.com/Spyou/Zangetsu): source code and issue tracker.

## Answering style

Users are usually non-technical and often frustrated. Be direct, give the exact menu path, and say
plainly when something is the source's fault rather than the app's. If a question is really "give me
a source", explain the empty-by-design position rather than apologising for it.
